name: pe_info
description: Read an executable's structure from its bytes without running it. PE: the DOS, COFF and optional headers (fields read within the optional header's declared size), the data directory table, sections with the entropy of their raw bytes and their permissions, import library and function names (a list longer than the answer holds is kept whole in a file), the export directory's image-name field, the COFF TimeDateStamp as its raw value and as a Unix time in UTC (a reading of a number: a reproducible build writes a hash there, not a compile time), and the certificate table's declaration (offset, size and the first entry's header: presence only, nothing is verified). ELF, 32- and 64-bit in either byte order: the header, program and section headers, and the dynamic array read through PT_DYNAMIC (DT_NEEDED, SONAME, RPATH, RUNPATH) with the interpreter; stripped is reported only when section headers show it. Mach-O: thin files in either width and byte order, and every slice of a universal binary (load commands, linked libraries, segments, entry offset, code-signature presence). Every answer, including a refusal, carries a status (complete, partial, failed or unsupported), the problems found, the limits hit and the structures read and not read. A table, segment, section or certificate range that runs past the end of the file is a problem (the file is truncated or the header is wrong), never a complete read. The tool has its own clock (max_seconds). A library path, search path or install name carrying user-info or a query value is withheld, with where it lies in the file. Not read: resources, export symbols, delay-load imports, TLS, CLR metadata, the Rich header, symbol tables, notes. No signature is verified, and size, entropy and import counts are triage features, not a determination of packing, intent or execution. An output directory reached through a symbolic link (the directory itself, work/ or the agent's directory under it, or $OUT/tool-output in a job) is refused and nothing is written through it. A stop signal (SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP) ends it with one JSON answer and the exit code 128 plus the signal from the moment the module has run as far as its stop handlers, which are installed at module level and not when main() starts (only the start of the interpreter and the compiling of the file come before); a second signal does nothing while the first is answered, and no hidden temporary file is left. A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings, from version 8: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential (a number, an array or a long Value too, and the NewValue after an OldValue), a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Before, only identifier-shaped strings (tokens, key ids, user-info) were withheld, so these were printed. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape.

path.description: A PE, ELF or Mach-O file

with_imports.description: Resolve imported function names as well as library names (default true)

limit.description: Rows of one table kept in the answer (default 5000: sections, segments, load commands, import functions); the whole of a longer table is written to a file under the tool-output directory and named

max_entropy_bytes.description: Work budget for section and segment entropy, in bytes measured (default 268435456, at most 4294967296); the pass also stops at max_seconds. A range left unmeasured says so

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds, from 1 to 110 (default 100); a read that reaches it stops, keeps what it read, and the answer is partial
